authors: Bauer, J., Fink, H., & Stoller, E.
title: Are issuer margins fairly stated? Evidence from the issuer estimated value for retail structured products
supports: The closest published work: verifies issuer-disclosed fair values with standard option pricing models on German retail certificates and concludes they can be reproduced. Its scope statement is the differentiation this paper rests on: Section 1 states verbatim that "More complex products like autocallables are left for future research". Sample is 714 single-asset DAX discount and capped bonus certificates, 3 to 24 month lifetimes, issued late September to October 2015, priced with Heston, practitioner Black-Scholes and Nadaraya-Watson, with hedging costs modelled as a barrier shift and option bid-ask spreads.
notes: Sections 1 to 4.5 read via the publisher's HTML on 2026-10-19. Results, conclusion and limitations were not reachable: the page text truncates inside Section 4.5 and the publisher's CDN refuses automated PDF requests, which was not worked around. The verifiable claims about this paper are therefore its question, scope, sample and method, not its reported replication errors. Obtain the PDF manually before citing any of its numerical results.

title: Callable barrier reverse convertible securities
supports: Published precedent for treating the ISSUER's early-redemption right in a barrier reverse convertible as an optimal-stopping problem rather than a barrier test, and for solving for the optimal policy explicitly. The abstract states the issuer "can call early redemption at any time during a pre-specified time interval", that the authors identify the optimal redemption policy, that for one asset it is a time-dependent boundary satisfying a nonlinear Volterra integral equation, and that for two assets it becomes a surface.
notes: Metadata verified on Crossref and on the SSRN record (Detemple, Boston University Questrom; Kitapbayev, Khalifa University; written January 2021, posted June 2021, forthcoming in Quantitative Finance). Full text not reachable: the publisher is paywalled and SSRN serves only the abstract page to automated requests, which was not worked around. Two scope limits follow and are differentiation points rather than problems: the method covers ONE OR TWO underlyings, where this paper's notes have three, and it is analytic/integral-equation based where this paper uses least-squares Monte Carlo. Do not attribute anything to this source beyond what the abstract states.

title: Finite-difference solution ansatz approach in least-squares Monte Carlo
supports: Least-squares Monte Carlo applied to worst-of issuer callable notes, the exact product class this paper prices. The preprint body corroborates three implementation choices independently: Section 2.2.4 uses a multi-variate LOCAL VOLATILITY model (Black-Scholes as its constant-vol special case) and Section 3.5 prices the worst-of notes under it; Section 2.1.1 treats the ISSUER's exercise as an infimum over stopping times with the sign flipped relative to holder exercise, solved by dynamic programming, which is the sign convention this project had to correct in its own payoff engine; and Section 2.2.2 frames the finite-difference ansatz as a control variate.
full_text_inspected: preprint body read; published version not inspected
notes: Published version is Journal of Computational Finance 2025, 10.21314/jcf.2025.008, and is paywalled and not inspected. The open preprint arXiv:2305.09166 was read instead (abstract plus Sections 2.1-2.2 and the Section 3.5 setup; Appendix A.2 and the Section 3.5 result tables were not reachable in the HTML render). Cite the published 2025 version for the record, but attribute any specific section claim to the preprint, since the two may differ. Verbatim from the preprint abstract: "Independent of model settings, the ansatz is proved to serve as a control variate."

authors: US Securities and Exchange Commission, Division of Corporation Finance
title: Sample letter sent to financial institutions regarding their structured note offerings disclosure in their prospectus supplements and Exchange Act reports
venue: SEC, Office of Capital Markets Trends
supports: The origin of the estimated-value disclosure this paper is built on. Signed by Amy M. Starr, Chief, April 2012. Asks that issuers "should consider prominently disclosing the difference between the public offering price of the note" and its estimated fair value.
notes: Read in full. Two corrections this forced: the disclosure is staff comment-letter GUIDANCE, not a rule, so the paper must not say the SEC requires it; and the letter contains no 'internal funding rate' language, which is the issuers' own wording in their supplements and must be attributed to the filings, not to the SEC.

title: 17 CFR 230.424 - Filing of prospectuses, number of copies (Rule 424(b)(2))
supports: The source of the calendar constraint. Rule 424(b)(2) requires the priced prospectus supplement to be filed "no later than the second business day following the earlier of the date of the determination of the offering price or the date it is first used after effectiveness". This is why an outside analyst can never hold pricing-date option data for a note whose final terms they learn from the filing.
notes: Deadline confirmed as business days from the regulation text, not from secondary description. Cite the eCFR current version with an access date.

title: Arbitrage-free SVI volatility surfaces
supports: Source of the raw SVI parameterisation in total implied variance and of both arbitrage conditions enforced here: the butterfly condition g(k) >= 0 and the requirement that total variance be non-decreasing in maturity.
notes: Published version, not the 2012 SSRN preprint (10.2139/ssrn.2033323), which is superseded. The log-moneyness/total-variance form the local-volatility step uses is the one set out here, which is why Dupire's 1994 Risk article is not cited: it has no Crossref deposit and could not be verified to the standard applied here.

title: No arbitrage SVI

notes: Published version, not the 2020 SSRN preprint (10.2139/ssrn.3594528). The DOI was confirmed as 10.1137/20m1351060; an earlier note in this project recorded 10.1137/20M1343090, which is wrong.

authors: Farkas, W., Ferrari, F., & Ulrych, U.
title: Pricing autocallables under local-stochastic volatility
verified_via: Crossref API; abstract read via RePEc working-paper listing
supports: Prices single-asset autocallable barrier reverse convertibles under Heston local-stochastic volatility against local volatility, and reports that LSV typically gives HIGHER prices, attributing this to forward-skew and vol-of-vol dependence. Also states the stochastic parameters control the autocallable price while leaving the fit to European options unaffected, which is why a European repricing gate cannot detect this dimension.
notes: Found during peer review, not during the original literature pass. Single-asset products, so the direction is adjacent to this paper's worst-of sample rather than transferable to it. Crossref returns a malformed author list with empty entries, so the authors field here is authoritative.

title: The interplay between stochastic volatility and correlations in equity autocallables
verified_via: Crossref API; abstract read via SSRN
supports: Studies equity WORST-OF autocallables under multi-dimensional stochastic local volatility and finds correlations between the stochastic variances are central to pricing and risk management. Supports the claim that correlation and surface dynamics are not separable candidates in this product class. The abstract gives no price direction, so no directional claim rests on it.
notes: Found during peer review. Cited only for the interaction, never for a direction.
